resources.string:
Lets ArcX read the text on your screen so a workflow can act on whatever you are looking at — summarise an article, explain an error, reply to a message — without you selecting or copying anything first.

Android only lets an app read the screen that is currently in front, and ArcX's own window covers yours while a workflow runs. So ArcX reads at two moments: once when you open a screen, and again when you open the ArcX bubble — there it may read a few times across about half a second, because some apps, browsers especially, take a moment to make their content readable. ArcX keeps only the most recent copy, in memory, for two minutes, and it never leaves your device on its own. ArcX does not follow along as you scroll or type.

A workflow whose input is your screen as a picture also captures an image of it. That image is sent to your AI provider and saved on this device so you can see it in History — the only screen content ArcX writes to storage. Images are kept for the period you choose under Privacy, and Clear history and Delete all local data remove them immediately.

Text you type into a password field is skipped. A password an app puts on screen as ordinary text — a Wi-Fi sharing screen, for instance — looks like any other text, and a picture of your screen shows whatever is on it. Only run these workflows on screens you are willing to share.

When you do run a workflow that uses the screen, that text is sent to the AI provider you configured in ArcX — so only enable this if you are comfortable with that provider seeing what is on screen.

You can turn this off here at any time; the copy in memory is dropped immediately. Every other part of ArcX keeps working without it.
